original_value: Vehicle detection is an indispensable part of environmental perception technology for smart cars. Aiming at the issues that conventional vehicle detection can be easily restricted by environmental conditions and cannot have accuracy and real-time performance, this article proposes a front vehicle detection algorithm for smart car based on improved SSD model. Single shot multibox detector (SSD) is one of the current mainstream object detection frameworks based on deep learning. This work first briefly introduces the SSD network model and analyzes and summarizes its problems and shortcomings in vehicle detection. Then, targeted improvements are performed to the SSD network model, including major advancements to the basic structure of the SSD model, the use of weighted mask in network training, and enhancement to the loss function. Finally, vehicle detection experiments are carried out on the basis of the KITTI vision benchmark suite and self-made vehicle dataset to observe the algorithm performance in different complicated environments and weather conditions. The test results based on the KITTI dataset show that the mAP value reaches 92.18%, and the average processing time per frame is 15 ms. Compared with the existing deep learning-based detection methods, the proposed algorithm can obtain accuracy and real-time performance simultaneously. Meanwhile, the algorithm has excellent robustness and environmental adaptability for complicated traffic environments and anti-jamming capabilities for bad weather conditions. These factors are of great significance to ensure the accurate and efficient operation of smart cars in real traffic scenarios and are beneficial to vastly reduce the incidence of traffic accidents and fully protect people’s lives and property.

result.paraphrase: Vehicle detection is a vital component of environmental perception technology for smart vehicles. To address the limitations of conventional vehicle detection, which is often constrained by environmental conditions and struggles to balance accuracy with real-time performance, this paper presents a front-vehicle detection algorithm for smart cars based on an improved SSD model. Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) is one of the mainstream deep learning-based object detection frameworks. The study first gives a brief introduction to the SSD network model and then analyzes and summarizes its shortcomings in vehicle detection. Next, targeted enhancements are made to the SSD network model, including substantial improvements to the SSD basic architecture, the adoption of weighted masks during network training, and optimization of the loss function. Finally, experiments are conducted on the KITTI vision benchmark suite and a self-built vehicle dataset to evaluate performance in various complex environments and weather conditions. Results on the KITTI dataset show an mAP of 92.18% and an average processing time of 15 ms per frame. Compared with existing deep learning-based detection methods, the proposed algorithm achieves both accuracy and real-time performance. At the same time, it demonstrates excellent robustness and environmental adaptability in complex traffic scenes as well as strong anti-interference capability under adverse weather conditions. These qualities are highly important for ensuring the accurate and efficient operation of smart cars in real traffic scenarios and help greatly reduce traffic accidents while protecting people’s lives and property.
